pages.main_text_excerpt:
We launched the Nivel platform in Bergen, Norway, in 2020. Later, we added more European cities and are now expanding internationally with the support of ambitious venture capital funds. Recently our team has been increased to cover German-, English-, Italian-speaking markets.
Our team assembles decades of experience delivering useful and innovative solutions at the intersection of the private and public sectors.
Harald Sævareid
Harald has been working on innovative solutions for the public and private sector since 2001. Before founding Nivel he was a Smart City Adviser to the city of Stavanger in Norway. He has also served as a board member for Kolumbus, the public transportation administration (PTA) of the Rogaland county in Norway, and has extensive experience from both sides of the table in public procurement processes. His passion is to create and design better cities, in close collaboration with businesses and citizens. harald@nivel.no +47 92081006
Sven Inge Bråten
Sven has been in the digital product development space for almost two decades, both as a product designer and product lead, and brings extensive experience to Nivel as head of product. Co-founding Nivel allowed him to combine his expertise with his interest in creating more livable cities around the world. Sven is heading the one person office in Oslo. sven@nivel.no
Patrick Ramberg Singler
Patrick leverages his experience helping Nordic companies scale internationally and his expertise in enterprise SaaS sales to expand Nivel’s reach. Passionate about building lasting partnerships, he combines hands-on market knowledge with a practical approach to growth across borders. Outside of work, you might find him exploring new destinations, savoring local food, or practicing martial arts—always bringing a blend of curiosity and discipline into his personal and professional life. patrick@nivel.no +49 151 29571162 +47 91531539
Marcin Wójcik
Marcin is a backend engineer specializing in clean architecture and scalable system design. With a background that spans programmer, Delivery Manager and Product Owner roles, he combines hands-on technical expertise with a strategic understanding of how products evolve and succeed. He has delivered solutions across diverse industries including AdTech, Industry 4.0 and shared mobility, translating complex business needs into robust, maintainable software. Marcin enjoys designing efficient systems, unblocking teams with practical guidance and ensuring engineering decisions support long-term product goals. Outside of work, he is a dedicated martial artist — a 4th-dan Aikido instructor who runs his own dojo where he applies the same focus and discipline that guide his work in tech. marcin@nivel.no
Maroof Mushtaq
Maroof specializes in Nivel's spatial analytics and data infrastructure. He transforms raw data into actionable insights through advanced geospatial analysis and data pipeline optimization, ensuring reliable, real-time insights into shared mobility services. Maroof holds a Master's in Data Science from the University of Stavanger, where his thesis explored limiting hallucinations in large language models using knowledge graphs - research conducted in partnership with Laerdal Medical. He brings a strong technical foundation spanning data science, machine learning, cloud platforms, and computer vision, complemented by leadership experience as former President of the Erasmus Student Network. Based in Stavanger, Maroof takes full advantage of the region's stunning natural landscapes through hiking and has recently taken up climbing. When not optimizing data pipelines or analyzing mobility patterns, you'll find him exploring mountain trails or learning new routes on the rock face. maroof@nivel.no
Braedon Rodenberg
Braedon develops Nivel’s analytics products and the data back-end to support them. He brings extensive experience working for private and public mobility projects in the US, Asia and Europe and hopes to make shared mobility convenient, accessible and unobtrusive for all. Braedon is based in Tokyo - taking full advantage of the city’s ultra-convenience while enjoying the beautiful nature just a stones throw away. His recent hobbies include sports yabusame (competitive horseback archery), going to hot springs and travelling with his wife and two children. He also teaches data and business analytics at Keio University’s business school. braedon@nivel.no
Finn Espen Gundersen
Finn Espen, civil engineer from NTH, has experience in buying and selling businesses, strategy, IT security, software sales, and developing reliable software systems. pages.main_text_excerpt:
Micromobility regulation
Frankfurt: Reducing clutter with a central management platform
Better micromobility parking with digital regulation
Nov 18, 2024
In Frankfurt, Germany, the city faces the challenge of managing 12,000 shared vehicles, including e-scooters and bikes, operated by multiple providers. Poor parking and vehicle clutter were common issues, complicating mobility for residents and creating disorganized streetscapes.
To tackle these challenges, Frankfurt implemented Nivel's digital regulation platform to enhance parking management and reduce clutter. By using insights on user behaviour, the city established designated parking areas based on actual demand, ensuring vehicles are available where they are most needed. This data-driven approach allowed the city to set clear parking rules that were digitally communicated to all operators, significantly shortening coordination time and ensuring consistent application of policies.
Nivel's platform also enabled officials to monitor compliance, track vehicle utilization, and adjust regulations dynamically as needs are changing. This has led to a more orderly public space, improved accessibility, and better parking management.
Frankfurt plans to expand the use of Nivel's platform to roll out 1,000 mobility stations across the city, supporting e-scooters, bikes, and car-sharing services. With tools such as overflow alerts, fleet size monitoring, and real-time analytics, the city aims to create a more efficient, less cluttered environment. These efforts are part of Frankfurt's broader strategy to integrate shared mobility into urban transport, encouraging a shift away from private car use and promoting cleaner, more liveable public spaces.
The solution was featured on the daily news, Hessenschau where the Frankfurt mobility councillor, Wolfgang Siefert talks about how they are using the Nivel platform, including the Poor parking app. Click on the image to watch the Nivel clip.
pages.title: Frankfurt: Reducing clutter with a central management platform

pages.main_text_excerpt:
We are now expanding internationally, and looking for bright people who want to join us to create tidier and more sustainable cities.
We offer part-time & full-time employment as well as freelance options
We do most work asynchronously and limit the number of meetings
We are conscious about communicating in a constructive and open manner
You’ll have a quick and continuous impact - we’re shipping and improving fast
We offer employees shareholder options, private health insurance and a decent pension scheme
We are still a small team, so you will get to know everyone quickly. At the moment we’re working distributed from Stavanger, Oslo, Tokyo, Berlin, Dortmund and other places.
You can work fully remotely, but we’re also happy to welcome you to our headquarters in Stavanger. We know many people who have come to Norway for the job but stayed for the great lifestyle. Here are some reasons:
Norway is indeed a paradise for skiing and snowboarding. One of our favourite spots is Lyngsheia, which is just a 1-hour drive away from our office in Stavanger where you can go back country skiing from January to May.
There are several world-class surf spots like Solastranden around Stavanger which you can reach in just 15 minutes by car from the office. Suit recommended!
The archipelago of Stavanger offers fantastic kayaking opportunities.
Stavanger is one of the most international cities in Norway and the sun sets at 22:30 in summer.
Weekends, holidays and even team building events are often spent in one of the 550 self-served mountain huts in Norway.
Alessandra, our Italian Policy Advisor talks about all outdoor activities you can do.
We try to make the hiring process as smooth and quick as possible, so you will usually hear from us within 7 - 14 days whether we would like to invite you for an interview.

Frankfurt: Reducing clutter with a central management platform

Micromobility regulation
Frankfurt: Reducing clutter with a central management platform
Better micromobility parking with digital regulation
Nov 18, 2024
In Frankfurt, Germany, the city faces the challenge of managing 12,000 shared vehicles, including e-scooters and bikes, operated by multiple providers. Poor parking and vehicle clutter were common issues, complicating mobility for residents and creating disorganized streetscapes.
To tackle these challenges, Frankfurt implemented Nivel's digital regulation platform to enhance parking management and reduce clutter. By using insights on user behaviour, the city established designated parking areas based on actual demand, ensuring vehicles are available where they are most needed. This data-driven approach allowed the city to set clear parking rules that were digitally communicated to all operators, significantly shortening coordination time and ensuring consistent application of policies.
Nivel's platform also enabled officials to monitor compliance, track vehicle utilization, and adjust regulations dynamically as needs are changing. This has led to a more orderly public space, improved accessibility, and better parking management.
Frankfurt plans to expand the use of Nivel's platform to roll out 1,000 mobility stations across the city, supporting e-scooters, bikes, and car-sharing services. With tools such as overflow alerts, fleet size monitoring, and real-time analytics, the city aims to create a more efficient, less cluttered environment. These efforts are part of Frankfurt's broader strategy to integrate shared mobility into urban transport, encouraging a shift away from private car use and promoting cleaner, more liveable public spaces.
The solution was featured on the daily news, Hessenschau where the Frankfurt mobility councillor, Wolfgang Siefert talks about how they are using the Nivel platform, including the Poor parking app. Click on the image to watch the Nivel clip.
